proof_natural:
**Proposition.** For a physical system S with state space Ω and dynamics governed by a measure μ, there exists a scale parameter ε₀ > 0 such that: (1) For scales ε < ε₀, the system admits only a discrete spectrum of observables with measure μ_d supported on a countable set, and (2) For scales ε ≫ ε₀, the effective dynamics is described by a continuous measure μ_c that is the weak limit of coarse-grained discrete measures.

**Proof.** Let Ω be a state space admitting a filtration {Ω_ε}_{ε>0} indexed by scale parameter ε. We assume there exists a fundamental scale ε₀ > 0 below which discreteness manifests, and that the observable algebras A_ε form a directed system with respect to scale. Further, we assume the dynamics preserves the scale hierarchy: for ε₁ < ε₂, the map π_{ε₂,ε₁}: A_{ε₁} → A_{ε₂} is a morphism. The measures μ_ε on Ω_ε satisfy the consistency condition π_{ε₂,ε₁}*μ_{ε₁} = μ_{ε₂}, where the coarse-graining map π_{ε₂,ε₁} is measure-preserving and surjective.

For scales ε < ε₀, by our assumption of discrete spectrum and the Spectral Theorem for self-adjoint operators, the measure μ_ε is purely atomic with support on a countable set D_ε ⊂ Ω_ε. This establishes the first part of our proposition.

To prove the second part, we define the coarse-graining operator R_ε: L²(Ω_{ε/n}, μ_{ε/n}) → L²(Ω_ε, μ_ε) for integer n > 1. The scale hierarchy and consistency condition ensure this operator is well-defined. 

For any bounded continuous function f on Ω_ε with ε > ε₀, the consistency condition combined with the Dominated Convergence Theorem implies there exists a sequence of discrete measures μ_n supported on D_{ε/n} such that ∫f dμ_n → ∫f dμ_ε as n → ∞.

[Note: To establish that the limiting measure μ_ε for ε ≫ ε₀ has continuous support requires additional structure on how discrete points accumulate under coarse-graining. This represents a gap in the current formulation.]

By Prokhorov's Theorem, the weak limit lim_{n→∞} R_n*μ_{ε₀/n} exists (at least along subsequences) and defines a measure μ_∞. The tightness required for Prokhorov's Theorem follows from the measure-preserving property of the coarse-graining maps.

For scales ε ≫ ε₀, the Stone-Weierstrass Theorem ensures that observables in the C*-algebra A_ε can be approximated arbitrarily well by continuous functions. Therefore, the effective dynamics at scale ε ≫ ε₀ is governed by the continuous measure μ_c := μ_∞, which is obtained as the weak limit of coarse-grained discrete measures.

This completes the proof. □

dependencies_literature.name: Spectral Theorem for Self-Adjoint Operators
dependencies_literature.statement: Every self-adjoint operator on a Hilbert space has a unique spectral decomposition
dependencies_literature.usage: Used to characterize discrete spectrum at small scales

dependencies_literature.name: Prokhorov's Theorem
dependencies_literature.statement: A family of probability measures on a complete separable metric space is relatively compact in the weak topology if and only if it is tight
dependencies_literature.usage: Guarantees existence of weak limit of coarse-grained measures

dependencies_literature.name: Stone-Weierstrass Theorem
dependencies_literature.statement: Continuous functions can uniformly approximate elements of certain subalgebras of C(X)
dependencies_literature.usage: Shows continuous functions approximate observables at large scales

dependencies_literature.name: Dominated Convergence Theorem
dependencies_literature.statement: For a sequence of measurable functions converging pointwise and dominated by an integrable function, the limit of integrals equals the integral of the limit
dependencies_literature.usage: Justifies interchange of limits in Step 3
